Definition: of Hebrew origin (H6726); Sion (i.e. Tsijon), a hill of Jerusalem; figuratively, the Church (militant or triumphant):--Sion.
BiblicalUsage: Sion is Zion, the hill of Jerusalem and the city of the living God, and the New Testament takes the name beyond the hill. The daughter of Sion is told her King comes meek on an ass, the stone is laid in Sion, a stumblingstone and rock of offence, and the writer to the Hebrews says we are come unto Mount Sion, the heavenly Jerusalem.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Zion is the city I have already come to, because the heavenly Jerusalem is not a distant hope but the assembly I belong to now.
